chapter: Kid Ory band personnel and repertoire
title: Personnel of the Ory band, 1958-60
summary: Front line, drummer Bobby Ozobin, forgotten piano and bass players, and the importance of good chords.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: who was in the Ori band.

At the time, I was in the Ori band and we're talking again the 1958 to 60 era. Boy, I'm about to draw a blank on the piano player, which was terrible. Let's see. Well, anyway, the front line was Ori, of course, trombone. I was playing trumpet. The clarinetist was either Bill Shea or Ellis Horn, who had been a veteran of the Lou Waters band. Bill Napier, for a short while, right before he went east to join Bob Scobie for one of Scobie's last major trips. Napier was very good, fit the band very well. And back of us, we had Bobby Ozobin, a very good drummer who had the opposite of Zutty, had a nice light touch, did indeed swing very well. And the Ori band just did not require an overpowering drummer because Ori played an ensemble driving tightness that was in itself a force and you didn't have to have volume to go along with it. And you could play very comfortably with the band and still have a lot of punch, you know, everybody's playing together and Bobby Ozobin fit very well with that group. He'd done some traveling, I know, with Ivory Joe Hunter in the 50s. I don't know what other groups. He was a California musician. That's really funny. I just can't think who the piano player might have been. We may have to turn the tape off
while I think that. No, we'll come to you.
We probably had a bass player and I can't think who that was right now.
Well, I hope the piano player played good chords.

Oh, I hope so because I certainly needed that because I didn't name chords by name but I sure relied on them to play on top of my own, what little ability I had, my intuitive and playing by ear. I could sure tell a bad chord when I heard it and I would get really frozen up if I heard a bad one coming at me. But if I heard good chords and some good rhythm, I sounded indeed better than I was. I'm just sorry I never had a chance to record with the Ori band but he did not do any recording in that period.
